legitimate_personal_agent_use.finding: comparing prices and ordering on the user's own account is personal use; the user is the customer.

peer_operator_risk.finding: Amazon has litigated exactly this traffic. a residential peer carrying signed-in agent sessions would be the network address Amazon sees, in a dispute where Amazon claims unauthorized computer access. no peer operator should carry that.

site_position.finding: Amazon sued Perplexity in November 2025 over the Comet agent shopping in signed-in accounts; a district court granted a preliminary injunction in March 2026; the Ninth Circuit vacated it in August 2026; the case continues. Amazon also blocked Meta's Muse agent (TechCrunch, 2026-10-06). the site plainly treats this traffic as abuse.

recommendation.rationale: decline for both scopes: Amazon treats personal-agent shopping as unauthorized access and is litigating it, so peers would carry legal and blocking risk. a user's agent can still reach Amazon over the user's own Solo egress, where blocking is surfaced honestly.
